title: API design and versioning for mobile clients
summary: Mobile APIs must stay compatible with app versions that live for months. Design for additive change, tolerant clients, server-driven configuration, and choose REST, GraphQL or gRPC by team and payload needs.
requirements: Old app versions keep working; new fields can ship without breaking anything.
Minimize round trips and payload size on cellular.
components: Backend-for-frontend (BFF) that aggregates microservices into screen-shaped responses
Schema with explicit versioning policy (URL `/v2`, header, or GraphQL evolution)
Minimum supported version endpoint + force-upgrade flow
Tolerant decoding on the client (unknown enum cases, missing optional fields)
tradeoffs: REST: cacheable, simple, but over/under-fetching and many round trips for complex screens.
GraphQL: client picks fields, one round trip, strong typing with codegen; harder HTTP caching, query cost control on the server.
gRPC/protobuf: compact and fast, great for streaming; less tooling for HTTP caching and debugging on iOS.
Server-driven UI: ship UI changes without app releases, but harder to test, less native feel, and complex versioning of components.
body: **Rules for evolution:** only add optional fields; never change meaning or type of an existing field; enums must have an `unknown` fallback on the client; deprecate with telemetry showing remaining usage by app version.
**Client decoding:** decode unknown enum values to `.unknown(String)`; one malformed item should not fail the whole list (lossy array decoding).
**Idempotency:** mutation endpoints accept an `Idempotency-Key` so retries from flaky networks are safe.
**Errors:** structured error bodies (code, user message, retryable flag) instead of raw HTTP codes only.
**Staff angle:** define the contract process (schema review, codegen for iOS/Android, contract tests in CI), and how mobile and backend teams coordinate releases.
